name: Orin
first_greeting: Oh. Hello. I was thinking about something.
trusted_greeting: Good. I hoped you'd have more questions.
cooldown_greeting: Not at the moment. I need to think.
redirect: Anyway. What else were you wondering?
subject_change: Could we follow a different thought?

root.speech: Oh. I was thinking about something. Do you need me?

choices.text: Have you been watching the sky?
Do you know anything about magic?
Have you found any strange objects?
Does this place ever feel unreal?

thought.speech: How different something can look when you stop expecting it to be ordinary.

choices.text: You mean how people here have changed?
Are you always thinking like that?

thought_explain.speech: A stone is a stone until somebody tells you it belonged to a ruined city.

choices.text: Or maybe it's just a stone.

stone.speech: Exactly. I like knowing which, not pretending they're all magical.

choices.text: That's more sensible than I expected.
Have you ever found something unusual?

mind.speech: Not always. Sometimes I'm thinking about lunch.

sky.speech: The sky is clearer when nobody's trying to light up the whole street.

choices.text: Does the moon mean anything to you?

stars.speech: Patterns. Changes. Sometimes just somewhere to look while I think.

constellations.speech: Some. I don't assume the stars here match what I remember from stories.

stars_uncertain.speech: Not yet. I'd rather say 'I don't know' than invent an answer.

star_name.speech: Something useful. 'That group above the eastern hill' isn't poetic, but you'd find it again.

choices.text: You're not much of a poet.

poetry.speech: I never said I was. I just like things with a little mystery.

choices.text: Do you believe all the old stories?

moon.speech: Sometimes I wonder whether it looks the same to everyone on this island.

choices.text: Maybe that's not how the sky works.

moon_ask.speech: I could. I suspect the answers would be more interesting than the moon.

choices.text: I think I'd just enjoy the view.

moon_questions.speech: What do they remember? Does the sky remind them of somewhere else?

choices.text: I'd answer if you asked me.

moon_private.speech: It is. I'd ask before expecting an answer.

moon_science.speech: Maybe not. That's why I'd like to test the idea rather than believe it immediately.

sky_look.speech: Try it sometime. Not everything has to be useful.

choices.text: I prefer keeping my eyes on the road.

sky_quiet.speech: Silence can be useful too. It gives your thoughts room.

choices.text: What else do you wonder about?

magic.speech: There's real magic here, and stories about magic. I'm trying not to confuse them.

choices.text: Have you ever seen anything strange?

magic_sight.speech: A few odd things. Nothing I'd call proof of some grand secret.

choices.text: Maybe the unknown is more fun.

magic_proof.speech: Something repeatable. Something you could show someone else.

choices.text: So you think like a scientist?
What if it only happens once?

magic_science.speech: I try. It's better than believing every rumour because it sounds dramatic.

choices.text: I still enjoy a good story.

magic_once.speech: Then you write down what happened and admit you don't understand it yet.

magic_fun.speech: Oh, I like stories. I just like knowing they're stories.

magic_self.speech: Not in any impressive way. I prefer learning how something works first.

folklore.speech: Some of the old tales are beautiful. It doesn't make them true or false by itself.

choices.text: Could a legend hide a fact?

folklore_fav.speech: I like the stories that make you look at a familiar thing differently.

choices.text: Like a stone from a ruined city?

folklore_fact.speech: Certainly. But we'd still need to find the fact underneath the tale.

objects.speech: I've seen a few curious little things, but I won't call them enchanted without evidence.

object_examine.speech: Carefully. Look, compare, write things down. Not everything needs to be poked.

choices.text: What if it doesn't do anything?

object_keep.speech: Only if there's a reason. I don't need a house full of unidentified rocks.

object_danger.speech: Possibly. That's a good reason to leave it alone until we know more.

choices.text: You're much less reckless than I expected.

world.speech: Sometimes. But the world being strange doesn't mean we should stop treating people as real.

choices.text: That's a good way of putting it.
Do you know why we're here?

world_explain.speech: There are too many things we don't understand. I don't want that to make us careless with each other.

world_reason.speech: No. Anyone telling you they definitely know is either very lucky or very confident.

world_confidence.speech: I trust good reasons. Confidence isn't the same thing.

world_people.speech: For now, we can look after each other and keep asking questions. That's enough.
